meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. My son found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it, or did he get the same treatment I did?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.

You didn't answer me, Hale: was Owen heard before the zero? And show me that line in the essay, the page it's on, because a misquote is a mistake students make every day. I'm writing it down: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile."
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. My daughter won her appeal, and you just tied my son to it with "it seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down word for word, and it's going to the principal today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that the remark about my family be retracted in writing, and that nothing is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, agreed to nothing.
What moved her: the quotation that isn't in Hamlet, briefly, before the Claire remark undid it.
